title: Introducing the Fibonacci Code Challenge
summary: Briefs the Fibonacci coding challenge: write fibonacciGenerator(n) that returns an array of the first n Fibonacci numbers. Lays out the checker's constraints and sketches the flowchart logic as a hint.

concepts.heading: The sequence
points: Begin with 0 and 1; every later term is the sum of the two terms before it (1+2=3, 2+3=5, 13+21=34 style).
This course's version always starts 0, 1 (other versions start at 1), so the first two entries are fixed.

concepts.heading: Function contract
points: Call shape: fibonacciGenerator(n), where n is how many items to produce.
The result is returned (not alerted, no prompt) as an array: fibonacciGenerator(3) gives [0, 1, 1]; fibonacciGenerator(5) gives five items [0, 1, 1, 2, 3].
It must also work for n = 1 ([0]), n = 2 ([0, 1]) and large n such as 245.
A variable (output) holds the returned array for testing: pass a number, run, inspect the array.

concepts.heading: Checker constraints in the exercise
points: Do not edit the existing scaffold code; the checker looks for the function name and calls it with a number.
Return a real array with square brackets and comma-separated numbers.
If using a for loop, declare the counter inside the header with var (for (var i = 0; ...)), not an undeclared i = 0, because the checker's JavaScript version demands it.
A while loop or any other approach is allowed.
An online sandbox is linked from the lesson for trying the code.

concepts.heading: Planning with a flowchart
points: The hard part is the logic, not the syntax. Draw it first (a tool such as draw.io works) and then turn it into code.
Flow: if n is 1, return [0]. If n is 2, return [0, 1]. These are the predefined starting values.
Otherwise start from the first values and add the last two items to get the next one, push it on the array.
After each addition compare the array length to n; if smaller, repeat; if equal, return the array.
Worked example n = 5: [0,1] then add 0+1 -> 3 items, add 1+1 -> 4 items, add 1+2 -> 5 items, stop.

task.name: Coding Exercise 7: Fibonacci
task.starting_point: A scaffold with a fibonacciGenerator(n) function stub and a variable that stores its output; do not alter these.
task.goal: Return an array containing the first n Fibonacci numbers.
steps: Loop, adding the last two entries and pushing the result, until the array has n items.
task.expected_result: fibonacciGenerator(5) returns [0, 1, 1, 2, 3]; works for n = 1, 2 and 245.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 15 - Intermediate Javascript/15.13 - Introducing the Fibonacci Code Challenge/script.js

pitfalls: Editing the scaffold, which breaks the checker.
Writing i = 0 without var in the for header.
(Extra) n = 0 is not covered by the lecture; return [] for it.
Reference repo diverges: it has a hard-coded 'var number = 1' and console.log call outside the function.

playground.coverage: Tasks, starter stub and a solution; notes stress edge cases and why the loop starts at 2.
gaps_and_ideas: Add the course's checker rules as tasks (return an array, do not alter the function name).
Add the flowchart idea: draw the decision for n = 1, n = 2, then loop, before coding.
Add n = 245 as a scale test and a note that numbers get large.
